_about: What's new in each version of Manifexus, newest first. Shown in Updates. Write for people, not developers: short, plain sentences about what they can now do. The newest entry's version is what gets built and tagged; older entries can give the "commit" they were released from.

releases.headline: Meet Ask Manifexus: a private AI, built in, that can look into problems and fix them with your OK.
new: Ask Manifexus. Tap Ask in the header and ask anything about your apps: why something stopped, what changed, what's using the most memory.
It runs on your own server. It's free and private, and nothing leaves your network.
Picked for your server. Manifexus checks your memory, processor and graphics card, and recommends AI models that fit without slowing your apps down.
Downloads that don't give up. If the connection drops, the AI download picks up where it stopped, even after a restart. Every download is checked before it's used.
Fix with AI. One tap from the To Fix list in Diagnostics, and it works out what's wrong.
You're always in control. Every change is shown to you first, with a before and after of every file. It's backed up, and you can undo it from Restore.
Choose how much it may do on its own: Look Only, Ask Before Changes, Fix Routine Things or Expert.
Learn how it's done. Turn on Show Commands (or choose Advanced in Settings) to see the command behind every step, with a plain explanation of each part.
Do It Myself. Every AI fix can be done by hand instead, one step at a time, with the terminal a tap away.
Activity → Commands. A learning log of every command behind your recent changes, and How It Was Done on every activity.
improved: Fix with AI has its own screen. It shows the problem, works on it step by step, then shows the change with a before and after of every file: Make Changes, Do It Myself or Not Now. After the change it runs the checks again to confirm the problem is gone. No chat box, no settings: one problem, start to finish.
Ask Manifexus starts a new chat every time you open it. Earlier chats are under Previous Chats (the clock), kept in your browser.
The message box only appears when it's your turn. While the AI works you just see what it's doing and a Stop button.

The AI knows what Manifexus can do. Ask "can you move kavita to a new stack?" and it offers a button that opens Move for kavita, instead of terminal steps. It asks you a short question when it needs a detail, and treats "can you…" as a request, not a question.

The AI chooses the model per question by its real speed on your server: when the smarter model is about as fast, it does everything. Thinking is kept short on slow processors unless the problem needs it.
If the AI can't come up with a change that checks out, it stops and explains instead of trying again and again, and it no longer repeats the same lookup.

Smarter AI recommendations for every server. Setup measures your server's memory speed in a second or two, combines it with its processor, graphics card and free memory, and recommends the smartest model that answers in a reasonable time there, with the reason and the expected answer time. Usually that's one model: a second is only suggested when it would be clearly faster.

Estimates that learn your server. Every answer measures how fast the model really reads and writes on your server, and corrects the estimates for the other models too, so recommendations and progress times get more accurate the more you use it.
Progress while the AI works now counts the whole step (loading, reading and writing), not just reading, so the time left is much closer to reality.
Removing every AI model starts setup again from the beginning, with fresh recommendations.
Faster reading of long questions, and less memory used while the AI works.

The AI reads much less before answering, so answers start sooner: logs are boiled down to errors, warnings and the latest lines with repeats merged (a noisy 31,000-character log becomes a few lines), settings files show only the lines around the setting in question, Diagnostics only shows problems, and its own instructions are shorter. The fix for a broken setting now reads about 40% less.
Each AI step shows what it read: its instructions, the conversation, and what it looked up.

A new setup for Ask Manifexus. The first time you tap Ask or Fix with AI, a few short steps walk you through it: pick the AI models (picked for your server), what it may do, what it may look at, and how hard it thinks. The download starts as soon as you pick the models and keeps going while you choose the rest.

New: choose what the AI may look at. App logs, files on your server, Activity and Restore, and server details can each be turned off (also in AI Settings). Passwords, tokens and keys are always hidden from it.

The recommended models download as one pipeline with one progress view: disk space is checked for all of them first, they download one after another (smallest first), and each is checked, loaded into memory and given a test answer while the next one downloads, so everything is ready sooner.

Every step of getting a model ready is shown as it happens, with download speed, time left, which part it's on, loading into memory, and a test answer that measures how fast it is on your server. If Ask was opened from Fix with AI, it starts on your problem as soon as it's ready.

While Ask Manifexus works, you see each step as it happens: what it looked up, which model is reading and how much, a progress bar with the time left, and how long every step took. When it's done, it folds into one line you can open again.

Much faster fixes. Manifexus looks up the obvious things (the file or app in question) before the AI starts, and small file changes are written as a one-line edit instead of the whole file, so a fix like a wrong setting takes one AI round instead of several.

Choose Automatically (new in AI Settings, on by default). Each request gets the right model and amount of thinking: quick questions stay quick, tricky problems go to the fixer and think it through, and if the quick helper gets stuck the fixer takes over. The fixer only runs when there's enough free memory at that moment.

Answers appear all at once when they're ready, instead of trickling in word by word, and they're nicely formatted: numbered steps, code blocks with a Copy button, tables and highlighted names and paths.
Speed estimates are measured on your own server after the first few answers, and the processor is counted by its real cores, so "answers in" times are closer to the truth.
Updates now show version numbers and notes like these, instead of build codes.
Activity has a new Fixes filter.
fixed: Undo Fix no longer says it failed when it actually put the file back.
Ask Manifexus no longer fails with "fetch failed" after 5 minutes when an answer takes a long time on a slow processor. If the AI engine really stops answering, you get a plain explanation.
Questions wait until setup is completely finished (every model downloaded, tested and the everyday model loaded into memory), so the right model can be chosen and nothing else slows the answer down.
The progress line no longer claims the AI has finished reading when it hasn't. Past the time estimate, it says so and keeps a moving bar.
The AI's look at recent Activity shows the real error messages instead of "[object Object]".
Removing an AI model no longer shows "Unexpected end of JSON input" when it actually worked, and tapping Remove on a model that's already gone isn't an error.

Questions to Ask Manifexus no longer stay "In progress" in Activity forever. Each one is listed as "Ask Manifexus: …" and ends as done, failed (with the reason) or stopped. There's a new AI Questions filter.
On phones, the dashboard no longer shifts sideways by a few pixels.
If an AI model can't download, you get a clear reason and a Try Again button.
Updating Manifexus keeps your settings, history, backups and AI models, even if no data folder was set up. Diagnostics now tells you if one is missing.

releases.headline: The first full release: move, restore and understand your Docker apps, all in one place.
new: Restore. Go back to before any move or delete. Every change keeps a backup, and restores can be undone too.
Activity. A complete record of everything Manifexus does, with the exact reason when something fails.
Diagnostics. Health checks in plain words, with a To Fix list that stays until each issue is fixed.
App Details. Every app's health, resources, storage, network and what it has printed, in one place.
Software updates that restore the previous version automatically if the new one doesn't start.
improved: One clean, consistent design throughout, with every screen the same size.
Settings save as you change them.
fixed: A leftover app entry in one stack can no longer break moving apps into it.
